requirements.title: Published degree requirements
requirements.summary: The department degree table gives 130–131 credits, its highlight and sample plan give 130, and free electives are 11 in the requirements versus 10 in the sample. These unresolved discrepancies remain explicit. College HSS and university completion policies are mapped separately into the same degree scope.

requirements.title: AI, ML and DS Depth: At least 12 credits from approved courses
requirements.summary: Listed approved pool. At least 12 credits; Lehigh defines credit values as semester hours.

requirements.title: AI, ML and DS Electives: At least 21 credits from approved list or CSE courses at 100 level or above
requirements.summary: Listed approved pool. At least 21 credits; Lehigh defines credit values as semester hours. The source also permits CSE courses at level 100 or above; this is an open eligibility predicate, subject to catalog standing, prerequisite and graduate-course petition rules.

requirements.title: Linear algebra alternatives
requirements.summary: MATH 205, MATH 241 or MATH 242; source group range 3–4 credits, not an individual course credit value.

requirements.title: Physics lecture and laboratory
requirements.summary: Five credits belong to the two-course group; individual credits remain null.

requirements.title: Additional natural science: 3 credits in a course that has another natural science course as a prerequisite
requirements.summary: Source-stated credit requirement; semester-hour value; applicable college/university policy notes accompany this allocation.

requirements.title: ECO 001 — Principles of Economics
requirements.summary: Required economics slot. The college catalog supplies the verified title and four credits; the department page’s repeated engineering title is not accepted.

requirements.title: First writing course alternatives
requirements.summary: WRT 001 or the college-approved WRT 003 multilingual option. Placement conditions apply. These occupy the existing first writing slot; the department page’s copied engineering label is corrected using the college/course catalogs.

requirements.title: Second writing course alternatives
requirements.summary: WRT 002 or the college-approved WRT 005 multilingual option, with its prerequisite. These occupy the existing second writing slot; the department page’s copied chemistry label is corrected using the college/course catalogs.

requirements.title: Courses satisfying the Engineering College's Advanced HSS requirements
requirements.summary: Source-stated credit requirement; semester-hour value; applicable college/university policy notes accompany this allocation.

requirements.title: Free Electives
requirements.summary: Source-stated credit requirement; semester-hour value; applicable college/university policy notes accompany this allocation.

requirements.title: Computing ethics overlap exclusion
requirements.summary: CSE 252 does not count toward the humanities/social-science requirement.

requirements.title: Advanced HSS distribution
requirements.summary: Complete at least three courses and 12 semester hours across eligible HE, SW, AL, or College of Health CGH/POPH categories. At least one course worth 3+ credits must be in each of two categories; at least one must carry HE or AL. Every course must be 2+ credits and letter graded. This is a designation-based eligibility rule, not a finite list. The AI/ML/DS-specific CSE 252 HSS exclusion still applies.

requirements.title: Free electives and work experience
requirements.summary: Free electives may use regular courses or up to six advanced ROTC credits. Successful professional work assignments may earn up to six free-elective credits through ENGR 200/160 with prescribed P/F grading; coordinate with the advisor. These permissions do not repair the AI/ML/DS page’s 11-credit versus sample-plan 10-credit discrepancy.

requirements.title: College basic HSS structure
requirements.summary: ECO 001 plus WRT 001 or WRT 003, plus WRT 002 or WRT 005: three courses and at least ten semester hours. The source’s course titles resolve the degree page’s copied engineering/chemistry labels. Multilingual alternatives retain their course placement/prerequisite conditions. These are the same basic HSS slots, not ten additional credits.

requirements.title: Semester credit hours and course eligibility
requirements.summary: Lehigh defines course credits as semester hours. Intermediate 100–199 courses are normally closed to freshmen without petition; 400-level graduate courses require an undergraduate petition. Course numbering/department restrictions still apply to the AI/ML/DS open CSE 100+ elective rule.

requirements.title: Prerequisite and corequisite compliance
requirements.summary: Maintain prerequisites before classes begin; obtain authorized online permission or demonstrate equivalent outside preparation for exceptions. The dean, registrar or instructor may drop unmet-prerequisite registrations. Corequisites are taken in the same semester. Missing individual prerequisite metadata in this atlas is not permission to enroll.

requirements.title: Degree time limit and military credit
requirements.summary: Complete both degree and university requirements within eight calendar years; petition SOS for up to one year’s exceptional leave. Basic military-science credits are additional to curriculum credits; at most six advanced military-science credits can apply.

requirements.title: Undergraduate residence alternatives
requirements.summary: Satisfy either 90 credits at Lehigh or 60 of the final 75 degree credits at Lehigh/in residency programs. Approved Lehigh Abroad and LVAIC cross-registration count; ordinary outside transfer credit does not establish residency.

requirements.title: Degree GPA and completion deadline
requirements.summary: Earn cumulative GPA at least 2.00 and complete all curriculum requirements and university financial obligations by noon on the Friday before conferral. Students remain responsible for checking the degree audit with their advisor.

requirements.title: Graduation application
requirements.summary: Undergraduates apply through Banner by December 1 for May, July 1 for August, or October 1 for January graduation. Late applications incur a fee; no application is accepted within three weeks of conferral. Missing application requires the next conferral date.

requirements.title: Course repeat and grade replacement
requirements.summary: At most three attempts, including withdrawals. Only the latest grade and associated credits count; replace GPA only by repeating the identical course for a final Lehigh grade. P/F repetition cannot replace the original grade, and overloads are not approved for repetition.

requirements.title: Optional pass/fail limits
requirements.summary: Optional P/F is limited to one eligible 100–399-level course per semester and six courses in a four-year career (eight in a five-year/two-degree program). Below-100 courses need a college petition; 400+ courses are excluded. It cannot satisfy major/minor or distribution requirements. Obtain advisor acknowledgment and choose by day 15 (prorated summer/winter); no retroactive change. Returning to letter grading still uses a lifetime P/F slot. Required P/F work-experience courses are a separate prescribed grading system.

requirements.title: Optional pass/fail course exclusions
requirements.summary: No Sociology or Anthropology course at level 100+ may be optional P/F. The catalog also excludes ANTH 140/COGS 140/MLL 140; ENGL 122,123,124,125,126,155,157,163,175,177,187,189,191,387; and PSYC 107,109/SSP 109,117,153/SSP 153,176. Course-specific college restrictions apply in addition to the major/distribution prohibition.

requirements.title: Transfer grades, equivalence and session limits
requirements.summary: Transfer requires accredited-institution coursework, department/college equivalency and rigor review, and at least C (not C−); P/F credit does not transfer. Credit cannot exceed original or equivalent Lehigh amounts or duplicate an existing equivalent. Summer transfer maximum is 16 credits and winter maximum 4. The registrar makes the final award; non-equivalent courses may receive approved general/elective credit and appropriate distribution attributes.

requirements.title: Transfer procedures and credit conversion
requirements.summary: Outside grades do not enter the Lehigh GPA or replace an existing grade; LVAIC has its stated exception. Quarter credits convert at 3:2 without partial credit; ECTS at 2:1, subject to registrar/equivalent-course caps. Full-time concurrent enrollment elsewhere requires advance SOS approval except LVAIC. Continuing education, correspondence, independent study, or courses shorter than three weeks/14 contact hours per credit need advance SOS petition approval. Pre-/post-matriculation college/department rules may differ.

requirements.title: Continuing-student CSE transfer eligibility
requirements.summary: For continuing students, transfer at most two required plus two elective CSE courses including AP/exam credit. Obtain term-specific advance approval. Letter grade must exceed C−; completed coursework must be within four years. A repeat elsewhere is eligible only after withdrawal or a Lehigh grade below C−. University/college requirements also apply.

requirements.title: CSE transfer institution, assessment and approval
requirements.summary: Required CSE transfers normally need an ABET-accredited program or CSE-approved abroad program; the department may approve equivalent rigor. Four-credit courses need at least seven weeks. Required-course replacements need 60% controlled proctored/in-person assessment without internet, phone, messaging or AI (limited instructor-approved aids allowed), or a preapproved CSE in-person validation exam within ten days of the next semester. Submit complete syllabus/assessment protocol, instructor details, code/title and intended term for faculty review and Associate Chair recommendation; the chair decides appeals.

notes: Current department page announces Fall 2026 start and publishes required, depth and general elective tables. It states 130 credits in the highlight and a 130–131-credit minimum in the requirements table.

ECO 001, WRT 001 and WRT 002 repeat earlier engineering/chemistry titles in the published table. Their codes and 4/3/3 credits are preserved in requirement notes; unverified titles are deliberately not materialized as course records.
MATH 205/241/242 is a 3–4-credit alternative group. PHY 011/012 is a five-credit group. Individual credits remain null where the main requirement table supplies only group credit values.
The 21-credit general elective requirement allows an open CSE 100+ range in addition to the listed approved pool. The full range and college advanced-HSS options are not expanded.
The table gives eleven free-elective credits; the sample plan lists four plus six. This source discrepancy needs department clarification. Computing ethics CSE 252 explicitly does not satisfy HSS.

Calendar, normalized credit units, prerequisites, descriptions and public course resources remain unverified. The sample plan is not treated as a mandatory course sequence or authoritative individual credit source for alternatives.

2026-10-11: current college/course catalogs resolve ECO001/WRT001/WRT002 names and verify WRT003/WRT005 alternatives with placement/prerequisites. The department page’s copied titles remain documented as discrepancies. College advanced HSS uses current HE/SW/AL or CGH/POPH categories, minimum three courses/12 credits, breadth and letter-grade rules. University and CSE transfer/completion policies are mapped. Published numeric total/free-elective conflicts and unconfirmed AI-depth/general-elective overlap keep this record partial.
